entities.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the singular verb וַיְבָרֶךְ. The God who created the sea creatures and birds in Genesis 1:21 now blesses them.

review.translation: [Then|0] [God|2] [blessed|0] [them|1], [saying|3], “[Be fruitful|4] [and multiply|5] [and fill|6] [the waters|8,7] [in the seas|9], [and|10] [let|11] [the bird|10]{s} [multiply|11] [on the land|12].”

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject, and אֹתָם (“them”) refers to the creatures. לֵאמֹר introduces the words of blessing, פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ (“be fruitful and multiply”).
analysis.morphology: Piel wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix.
analysis.sense: to bless living creatures with fruitfulness

draft.change: Add Genesis 1:22 as an example of the object-pronoun sense in the existing et article.
draft.definition: With a pronominal suffix, אֵת expresses the direct object of a verb as a separate word.
draft.evidence: Genesis 1:22 uses אֹתָם for the creatures God blessed. The third-person plural suffix refers back to the creatures named in Genesis 1:21.

analysis.evidence: In וַיְבָרֶךְ אֹתָם אֱלֹהִים, “God blessed them,” אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיְבָרֶךְ. The suffix on אֹתָם identifies the water creatures and birds of Genesis 1:21 as the direct object. The blessing that follows speaks of both groups multiplying.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle in its suffixed form אֹת־ with the third-person masculine plural pronominal suffix ־ָם.
analysis.sense: with suffixes: me, you, him, her, us, them

analysis.evidence: In וַיְבָרֶךְ אֹתָם אֱלֹהִים (“God blessed them”), אֹתָם is the direct object. אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the third-person masculine singular verb וַיְבָרֶךְ, identifying God as the one who blesses.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute common noun with no prefix or suffix. It takes singular verbal agreement here.

analysis.evidence: לֵאמֹר introduces the words of God's blessing. The imperatives פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ (“be fruitful and multiply”) open the direct speech.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct with prefixed preposition לְ

analysis.evidence: God addresses the creatures directly. The paired commands פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ, “be fruitful and multiply,” link producing offspring with increasing in number so that the creatures fill the waters.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperative, second person masculine plural. Final וּ marks the plural imperative.

analysis.evidence: God addresses the creatures with three plural commands. וּרְבוּ follows פְּרוּ “be fruitful” and precedes וּמִלְאוּ אֶת־הַמַּיִם “and fill the waters.” The sequence shows that the creatures are to increase in number.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ־ joins רְבוּ, a second-person masculine plural Qal imperative, to the preceding command.

analysis.evidence: וּמִלְאוּ continues the plural commands פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ ‘be fruitful and multiply’. The direct object אֶת־הַמַּיִם ‘the waters’ identifies what the creatures are to fill as they multiply.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperative, second person masculine plural, with prefixed conjunction וּ־ ‘and’.

analysis.evidence: In וּמִלְאוּ אֶת הַמַּיִם, “and fill the waters,” אֶת marks הַמַּיִם (“the waters”) as the definite direct object of the imperative וּמִלְאוּ.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add Genesis 1:22 as an example of the existing sense “a body or flow of water.”
draft.definition: The waters of the seas that aquatic creatures inhabit.
draft.evidence: Genesis 1:22 commands the creatures to fill הַמַּיִם and locates those waters בַּיַּמִּים, “in the seas.”

analysis.evidence: In וּמִלְאוּ אֶת הַמַּיִם, “and fill the waters,” אֶת marks the waters as the direct object of “fill.” The following בַּיַּמִּים, “in the seas,” identifies the waters where the creatures are to multiply.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural noun in the absolute state, with the prefixed definite article הַ־ doubling the initial מ.
analysis.sense: a body or flow of water

analysis.evidence: In וּמִלְאוּ אֶת הַמַּיִם בַּיַּמִּים, the creatures are to fill the waters. בַּיַּמִּים locates those waters in the seas, just as בָּאָרֶץ gives the place where the birds are to multiply.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ with the definite article הַ (combined בַּ), followed by a masculine plural absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: In וְהָעוֹף יִרֶב בָּאָרֶץ, “and let the birds multiply on the earth,” the singular verb יִרֶב agrees with the collective noun עוֹף. The blessing distinguishes the birds from the creatures addressed in the command to fill the waters.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ plus definite article הָ plus a masculine singular absolute noun used collectively.

analysis.evidence: יִרֶב agrees with the singular collective הָעוֹף, “the birds,” and echoes וּרְבוּ, “multiply,” earlier in the same blessing.
analysis.morphology: Shortened Qal jussive, third person masculine singular.

analysis.evidence: The blessing tells aquatic creatures to fill הַמַּיִם בַּיַּמִּים, “the waters in the seas,” and birds to multiply בָּאָרֶץ, “on the land.” The parallel clauses distinguish land from sea.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ with the definite article, followed by a singular absolute noun.
